newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CNA Gallo jumps after restructuring news.
newsitem.headline: CNA Gallo jumps after restructuring news.

text.p: News that leading South African retailer CNA Gallo Ltd was mulling a restructuring of its retail and entertainment businesses cheered its share price in active trade on Monday, dealers and analysts said.
The share jumped to 400 cents at one point before retreating slightly on profit-taking. At 1200 GMT it was 18 cents higher at 390 cents and 166,300 shares had changed hands.

CNA Gallo is a diverse holding and investment company with with interests in specialist book stores, music software manufacturing and distribution, stationery products, film and video distibution and cinema.

"The restructuring is seen as positive on the stores side. Its stores business is very mature. Developing its other interests is seen as positive too which means it's positive for the share price," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
CNA Gallo announced earlier on Monday that it was considering a restructuring to more effectively capitalise on opportunities for growth of its entertainment and leisure activities.
CNA Gallo was undergoing a refocus and may be considering splitting its entertainment business from its stores, dealers said.
They said the company seeemed to be moving away from its established book, magazine and stationery stores and into more entertainment-oriented operations, targeting a younger market.
"If you look at CNA, it's really refocusing its whole operation away from books and towards the youngsters," said Societe Generale Frankel Pollak's David Shapiro.
"Its Netware software is doing very well. It's done a deal with Sweets From Heaven and next it will move into music, maybe try to recapture the music market," he added.

Sweets From Heaven in January made a deal with CNA Gallo under which it would franchise its outlets in CNA branches and Nu Metro cinema complexes throughout South Africa. CNA has a 25 percent stake in the sweet firm.
